Here are three facts about lighthouses:
1. Many lighthouses have distinctive light patterns, known as "characteristics," to help navigators identify which lighthouse they are seeing at night.
2. The tallest lighthouse in the world is the Jeddah Light in Saudi Arabia, standing at 133 meters (436 feet) tall.
3. Early lighthouses used oil lamps or candles, but most modern lighthouses now use electricity and automated systems.
